results.label: this tree ships the clean-rep count (src/challenge.js) (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the analytics payload carries the clean-rep count for the account it analyses
an unstarted count is served on the payload as `not_started` with `counted:null`, the DEFAULT 21 target and no failed-trade tally
and it is served for the SAME account the payload analyses, with the module’s version on it
a real journalled trade taken BEFORE the start day does NOT make the count zero: it stays unstarted, and the trade is visible in the window tally as history rather than as a failed rep
a target that is not a whole number 1–999 is refused by the settings route with the module’s own code, and nothing is stored
and so is a start that is not a real UTC date
a valid start and target are saved as the trader’s own settings and the count begins from the NEXT payload, not retroactively
a trade closed on the current UTC day, linked to the trader’s own plan, checklist-clean and journalled through the app is COUNTED, and the count is a count of trades
an unlinked trade is not a rep and says `plan_linked`
a link to a plan the trader does NOT own is not a plan link either: ownership is re-read on the way out, so a foreign id in the column buys nothing
a recorded FAILED checklist item is a recorded breach: the trade is not counted even though its plan link and its journal are fine
a trade with NO recorded checklist at all is not counted either — no record is not a clean record — and the payload counts those trades by name

a RECORDED decision not to honour the stop is a breach on its own, with every checklist item passed — and it is the trader’s own self-reported, hash-stamped acknowledgement that says so, which the payload states
and the row really carries that decision as the app stores it (0, self_reported, with the review hash), so the criterion reads a recorded fact and not an inference
a COMPLETE journal whose acknowledgement landed on the next UTC day is still not a rep, and the payload says which criterion failed rather than calling the trade unclean
a closed trade with NO journal acknowledgement waits rather than counts, and the payload reports it as waiting with the app’s own missing-field list
the count carries NO amount and NO goal figure, while the payload it rides on does report P&L — so the absence is the count’s choice, not the payload’s
and the other trader’s stored settings are their own: their count is unstarted with the default target while this trader’s stands at three
a rep on ANOTHER desk is not counted on this desk’s payload, and that desk’s own payload DOES count it: the count is scoped to the account the payload analyses, like every other figure on it
narrowing the page’s date filter does NOT narrow the challenge window: the start day is the window the trader declared, so a record cannot be made to look smaller by a filter
the start cannot be moved once closed trades sit in its window: BOTH a later and an earlier start are refused with 409 and the number of trades in the way
re-sending the SAME start is accepted (a settings screen that posts the whole form must not be locked out of saving), and the count is unchanged
moving the target changes the target and NOT the count, the run, or a single trade’s verdict
clearing the start is refused for the same reason as moving it: un-starting a count that has trades in it would erase a record
the settings screen’s own payload shape is preserved: an ordinary settings save still returns the settings it saved
reading the count TWICE changes not one byte of any table, index or trigger in the database — the read is a read
and the count cannot influence a decision: the payload’s limits say read-only with zero writes and no influence on grades, caps, permissions, guardrail decisions or plan changes
the milestone added NO table of its own: the declarations live in the users’ settings and nowhere else
and the two declarations are exactly two keys in that settings object, each of them an explicit value the trader set

scope: M115 api: the rep count over the real routes, its declarations and its read-only proof: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
